title: Fitting subscheme complement is the bounded-generator locus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For $r\geq0$, let $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be the $r$-th Fitting ideal sheaf of $\mathcal F$: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ with $M=\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, a surjection $A^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow M$ and kernel $K$, it is the ideal generated by the $(n-r)\times(n-r)$ minors of the $(n-r)\times n$ matrices whose rows lie in $K$ (the unit ideal when $r\geq n$); these ideals do not depend on the surjection and commute with localization [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], so they glue. Let $Z_r\hookrightarrow S$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$. Then: (1) for every $S$-scheme $T$, the pullback $\mathcal F_T$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is locally generated by at most $r$ sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] (every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood on which at most $r$ sections generate it) if and only if the structure morphism $T\to S$ factors through the open subscheme $S\setminus|Z_r|$; (2) for every $s\in S$ the following are equivalent: $s\notin|Z_r|$, i.e. $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)_s=\mathcal O_{S,s}$; $\mathcal F$ can be generated by at most $r$ sections on an open neighbourhood of $s$; the stalk $\mathcal F_s$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements as an $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-module.

source.place: Tag 0C3F (divisors-lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally) and Tag 05P8 (divisors-lemma-locally-free-rank-r-pullback) part (2), using More on Algebra Tag 07ZC (more-algebra-lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally) (1)<=>(3) for the stalk clause

proof.text: Work on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $s$, with prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), $M=\mathcal F(U)$ is a finite $A$-module; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3), $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$. The germ localization of [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization] identifies $\mathcal F_s$ with $M_{\mathfrak p}$. Write $I=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)$ using the chosen finite surjection $A^n\twoheadrightarrow M$. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](2), its base change to $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is $IA_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M_{\mathfrak p})$. Applied to the quasi-coherent Fitting ideal sheaf, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] says exactly that $s\notin|Z_r|$ is equivalent to $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and to $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)_s=\mathcal O_{S,s}$.

source.place: 0C3C (section-fitting-ideals), 0C3F (lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally); affine identifications from Schemes 01IA and 01HV, finite generation from Properties 01PB

Some generating $a$-minor $\delta$ of $I$ is outside $\mathfrak p$, since if every such minor lay in the prime then their generated ideal would lie in it. Choose the $a$ kernel rows giving this minor and reorder the $n$ generator coordinates so that these rows form a matrix $(C\ D)$ with $C$ square of size $a$ and $\det C=\delta$ (up to sign, which does not change $D(\delta)$). source.place: 07ZC (lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally), direct kernel-minor proof of (1) implies (4) instead of the residue-field/Nakayama argument; adjugate identity as in Algebra 07DQ

proof.text: Generation by at most $r$ sections on a neighbourhood implies generation of the stalk by their germs: a local expression as a linear combination passes to the same expression in germs. Conversely, if $M_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal F_s$ is generated by at most $r$ elements, pad the list by zeros to obtain a surjection $A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r}\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}$. For this presentation the $r$th Fitting ideal is the unit ideal by the $n\le r$ convention. Presentation independence in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](1) equates it with the ideal of the localized original presentation, which is $IA_{\mathfrak p}$ by Step 1. Thus this stalk ideal is the whole local ring and $s\notin|Z_r|$ by Step 1. This closes the three implications of clause (2), without a finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: 07ZC (1), (3), (4), with independence 07Z8 and base change 07ZA(3); Divisors 0C3F

proof.text: Now let $g:T\to S$ be any morphism. Cover $T$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$, and use the ring homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ induced by $g$. The affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] identifies $\mathcal F_T|_V$ with $\widetilde{B\otimes_A M}$, where $M=\mathcal F(U)$ as in Step 1. This module is finite: if $m_1,\ldots,m_n$ generate $M$, then $1\otimes m_1,\ldots,1\otimes m_n$ generate it, since $b\otimes\sum a_i m_i=\sum b\varphi(a_i)(1\otimes m_i)$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a) show that $\mathcal F_T$ is again finite type and quasi-coherent. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](2), the ideal on $V$ is $\operatorname{Fit}_r(B\otimes_A M)=\varphi(I)B$, where $I=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)$; the change in tensor-factor order is the map $b\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes b$ with its evident inverse. This proves the needed Fitting base-change formula on each affine chart, without any flatness assumption on $g$.

source.place: 0C3D (lemma-base-change-fitting-ideal), proved on affine charts by More on Algebra 07ZA(3); Schemes 01I9(1)

proof.text: For $t\in V$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q\subset B$, its image $s=g(t)$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Then $\varphi(I)B\subseteq\mathfrak q$ if and only if $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$: one direction tests $\varphi(a)$ for $a\in I$, and the other uses that $\mathfrak q$ is an ideal and therefore contains every finite $B$-linear combination of these images. By Step 4 and clause (2), already proved in Steps 1-3 and applicable to $\mathcal F_T$, local generation by at most $r$ sections at $t$ is therefore equivalent to $g(t)\notin|Z_r|$. Such neighbourhoods cover $T$ exactly when $g(T)\subseteq S\setminus|Z_r|$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] makes this image containment equivalent to a (unique) factorization of $g$ through the open subscheme $S\setminus|Z_r|$. The reverse implication from a factorization to image containment is immediate by composing its underlying maps. This is clause (1).
